title: Count through elapsed time, then give the number a human meaning

motion.summary: Large numerals advance through the hundreds inside a clock ring, reach 600, then recede in contrast while the lyric names Noah and his age.
phases: Present a number and a small unit label with no competing sentence.
Advance through clearly different values against a timekeeping ring.
Hold the destination number and make it subordinate as the human statement arrives.
motion.transferablePrinciple: Use a changing measure to make scale felt before the narrative explains whom or what that scale belongs to.
variations: Count accumulated footsteps, generations, rainfall, or distance only when the story supports the unit.
Build a field of objects instead of digits, then reveal one person within the scale.
Let a duration resolve into a date or a place rather than a character.
cautions: The intermediate count is an animation, not newly asserted historical events.
Check that the final value and unit come from the source material.
Avoid filling every instrumental gap with another counter.

quality.reviewer: agent visual inspection of decoded frame sequence
strengths: The huge measure creates a clear first focal point.
The shift from number to person creates a two-stage reveal instead of a static fact card.
limitations: The gray numeric layer has intentionally modest contrast on a very dark background.
Six stills show distinct count states, not the full cadence between them.
Observed from six decoded frames of the exact hashed MP4; this is a concept reference, not full motion, audio-sync or whole-film acceptance.
